script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for September 20. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Every living thing does one thing above all else: make more of itself.  Oak trees make acorns.  Bacteria divide.

Some species produce millions of offspring with no care. Others produce few with intensive investment. Both strategies work in different contexts. How you reproduce matters as much as whether you do. Reproduction costs—energy, resources, sometimes life itself.  The salmon dies after spawning.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Everything that persists has a way to reproduce itself.  Continuation requires creating the next generation—of offspring, ideas, or impact.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Legacy Planning - What Do You Reproduce?.

Here's your activity: What do you want to persist beyond your individual existence—children, ideas, values, skills, organizations? How are you actively reproducing these things? Legacy is reproductive success. What's your strategy? This helps you identify what to pass on beyond yourself.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how life makes more life can be applied to legacy planning - what do you reproduce?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
